conviction_note: Interims are a real event with a likely guidance touch (narrowing, FS revision, the first continuing-ops restatement after the Argos disposal), so abs_move is set at 5.0, above the 3.68 history median. The lean is only 55: Worldpanel puts Q2 grocery growth above the trimmed broker bar and Tesco raised its floor, but an 8.3% 20-day run-up and a weak Worldpanel start to H2 cut against it. The +0.7 findings sum and the +0.5 scaled number agree in sign and size.

already_public.what: Q1 (16 weeks to 20 June 2026): Sainsbury's sales +3.1%, grocery +3.6%, GM&C -3.7%, Argos -0.5%, LFL ex fuel +2.1%; FY27 total underlying operating profit guide of £975m-£1,075m and retail FCF >£500m reiterated
Argos sale to Swift Partners for at least £120m, completion expected Feb 2027, broadly neutral to underlying operating profit, ~£350m non-cash impairment, FY27 guide reiterated again
First £200m tranche of the £300m FY27 buyback completed 24 July; £100m of the guided programme remains
FY27 guidance detail: net finance costs ~£320m, tax ~29%, capex £800-850m, £300m buyback; FS no longer a separate segment

new_in_release.expect: H1 underlying operating profit (continuing ops, Argos in discontinued) against a ~£525-530m broker bar; Q2 sales are NOT pre-released. Worldpanel points to Q2 grocery growth at or above Q1, against a broker expectation of a slowdown to ~2.6%. Lean: slightly positive.

FY27 £975m-£1,075m likely narrowed (Deutsche) and restated for continuing ops, with FS guidance revised (Shore). Consensus of £1,054-1,061m already sits near the top of the range, so a narrowing to the upper half is roughly priced. Only a top end above £1,075m would surprise. Direction unknown, lean slightly positive.
Current-trading comment on the first weeks of H2. Worldpanel's 12 weeks to 4 October slowed to +1.3% with a 0.1pp share loss, which implies roughly flat September sales. Lean negative.
Interim dividend and the remaining £100m buyback tranche, which is inside guidance. An upsizing like Tesco's is possible but unsourced.
unknown: H1 retail FCF and working capital, plus Argos separation costs

bar: H1 underlying EBIT ~£525m ex-Argos (Shore Capital, via https://www.asktraders.com/analysis/sainsburys-h1-earnings-preview-shore-capital-says-full-year-forecasts-well-underpinned/ ; Deutsche Bank £525m, +3.1%) and ~£530m (Barclays, via https://britbrief.co.uk/business/acquisitions/sainsburys-strategy-in-focus-after-morrisons-talks-reports.html), with Barclays Q2 sales growth at 2.6%. FY27 company-compiled consensus (2 Oct) of £1.054bn continuing ops (https://www.ig.com/uk/news-and-trade-ideas/sainsbury-s-results-preview--can-grocery-growth-deliver-stronger-261014) against the company guide of £975m-£1,075m. Two agreeing broker sources plus company consensus, so the bar is sourced.

findings.finding: Worldpanel's 12-week Sainsbury's sales growth accelerated through the Q2 window, from +2.0% (to 14 Jun) to +2.9% (to 6 Sep, against market +2.0% on the 4-week read and flat share). Brokers expect Q2 to slow to ~2.6% from Q1's 3.6% grocery. In Q1 the company's own grocery print ran about 1.5pp above Worldpanel, so Q2 grocery growth plausibly lands at or above Q1 rather than below it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 on 30 Jun 2026: sales slowed less than forecast with the guide held, +1.27%. Interims Nov 2025: sales and profit beat plus guidance raise, +5.52%.
findings.why_not_priced: Brokers trimmed grocery sales forecasts (Deutsche, Citi) and Barclays sits at 2.6%, below the Worldpanel run-rate. If the market had taken the panel at face value, previews would carry ~3%+ Q2 grocery and Shore would not flag a 'quieter second half of the period'. It is a proxy and the company-to-panel mapping is loose, hence the size.
findings.independence: Worldpanel 12 weeks to 14 Jun 2026, Sainsbury's +2.0% (https://www.globalbankingandfinance.com/uk-grocery-inflation-slows-easing-fears-iran-war-hit/), against company Q1 grocery +3.6% (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/sainsbury-j---sbry/trading-statement/9642984). Same panel provider, so not fully independent.

findings.finding: The first weeks of H2 look soft. Worldpanel's 12 weeks to 4 October 2026 show Sainsbury's at +1.3% with share down 0.1pp (15.2% vs 15.3%), against +2.9% in the 12 weeks to 6 September, which implies roughly flat sales in September against a 4-week market of +1.0%. The current-trading line could therefore drop the 'outperforming the market' claim.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: When the outlook or current trading disappointed: Jan 2026 Christmas trading statement -5.29%, Apr 2026 prelims with the first FY27 guide -3.68%.
findings.why_not_priced: The data has been public since 13 Oct, and the stock rose from ~352p (16 Oct) to 361p since, so the market has so far looked through it, focusing on Tesco's raised floor. The implied September figure is an inference from two overlapping windows, not a published number. Shorts building into the print already point this way, so the finding is kept small.
findings.independence: NIQ's 12 weeks to 3 Oct show Sainsbury's +0.7%, share -0.2pp (https://andrewdremin.com/uk-grocery-share-worldpanel-vs-niq/, secondary blog).

findings.finding: Peer read-across and guide position: Tesco raised the floor of its FY27 profit guide to £3.15-3.30bn and lifted its buyback to £950m on 8 Oct. For Sainsbury's, company-compiled consensus of £1.054bn already sits near the top of the £975m-£1,075m range and Deutsche expects a narrowing. The release is the first restated on continuing ops (Argos discontinued, FY26 Argos profit £9m), so a guide narrowed to the upper half is likely but mostly expected.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 2025 interims raised the FY guide to >£1bn and added a special dividend, +5.52%. Apr 2026 first FY27 guide of £975m-£1,075m, -3.68%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the 8.3% 20-day run-up (from a ~320p early-October low) is the Tesco read-through, so this only pays if Sainsbury's lifts the top end above £1,075m or narrows above consensus. A guide merely narrowed around £1,050m would read flat.
findings.independence: Shore Capital: FY 'well underpinned', FY EBIT £1,070m near the top of the range (https://www.asktraders.com/analysis/sainsburys-h1-earnings-preview-shore-capital-says-full-year-forecasts-well-underpinned/). Deutsche expects narrowing (same preview set).

findings.finding: £100m of the guided £300m FY27 buyback remains after the first £200m tranche completed on 24 July, and no buyback RNS has been filed since. A second tranche is likely announced with the interims, but it sits inside what was already guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 2025: £150m buyback addition plus £250m special dividend, inside a +5.52% day that also carried a guide raise.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside guidance, so it is near zero. Only an upsizing (Tesco did one) would be new, and the Argos proceeds are offset by separation costs per the 31 Jul RNS, so there is no visible funding for one.

baseline_tension: Mixed. The +8.3% 20-day run-up and the +2.4 priced lean (from the 6.73% short) already price the Tesco read-through that the positive findings rest on, while the soft-H2 Worldpanel read agrees with the slightly building short. Net the findings sit only mildly above zero, so p_up stays at 55.
language_note: nothing the English sources did not already carry: the domestic RNS feed (Investegate) supplied the primary documents (Q1 statement, Argos RNS, buyback tranche completion) that the wire previews summarise, but no domestic trade-press or regional item added information beyond the international previews
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' / 'too small about the move': abs_move_pct raised from 4.5 to 5.0. A guidance touch (narrowing, FS revision, first continuing-ops restatement) is likely and Q2 sales are not pre-released. Not raised to the 7-9% small-cap base, given a FTSE 100 name with 16% realised vol.
'A narrow proxy loses to a broad series': the Worldpanel-based Q2 sales finding was trimmed from +0.8 to +0.7, because the company-to-panel mapping is inferred from one quarter.
'Positioning is the thing to beat': the soft-H2 negative agrees with a building short, so it was trimmed from -0.6 to -0.5.
Run-up already reflects the Tesco read-through: the guidance finding was trimmed from +0.5 to +0.4.
'A finding about a number already told is worth 0': checked, and no Q2/H1 pre-release exists. The buyback finding stays at +0.1 because it is inside guidance.
